title: Research: prove four-root minimum for seven-source paired-call connectors
body:
This proves that **four dirty root rows are necessary and sufficient for all 127 seven-source masks when every source and output map is called exactly twice**. It settles the seven-source root-minimum question explicitly left open in [PR2182](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/2182), pinned at `dc252de1cc594829c3031abdb4de104713bc474a`.

The new result is the three-root exclusion. The attaining four-root star is credited to PR2182, independently replayed here, and not claimed as a new construction.

## Proof and scope

The model has immutable sources, arbitrary initial root/target dirt, independent fixed F2-linear child maps, unobserved output targets, arbitrary invertible **scalar F2 root-row frames**, and per-occurrence child ports. The proof allows arbitrarily many frame changes. It normalizes each twice-called source to one axis, uses the all-ones output to place all axes in a four-point affine plane, and derives mandatory prefix-difference masks.

Two separately written engines exhaust **135,135 paired source words × 651 class partitions = 87,972,885 cases**. Every case misses mandatory masks; the smallest deficit is four. The C++ matching/prefix/incidence engine and Python restricted-growth/interval/subset-product engine agree on every histogram. The registered replay recomputes the complete Python census.

The inherited attaining program has **4 roots, 14 B calls, 254 A calls, and 56 paid root XORs**. A literal witness and complete symbolic cost expression accompany the proof. No total-tariff optimum, physical caller admission, new supplier, kappa improvement, or proof-assistant verification is claimed. Extra child calls, clean roots, target feedback, and matrix-valued intra-row transformations are outside the exclusion.

## Validation

On macOS arm64, CPython 3.12.14 and Apple Clang:

- Fresh Python/C++ census agreement; registered package replay and metadata/source-pin checks pass.
- Formal dirty-state forward/inverse replay and 4,362 concrete basis columns across 18 rectangular/singular-map cases pass.
- All 324 single-operation omissions and five additional mutations reject; six-source, neutral-transfer and odd-incidence controls pass.
- Read-only, no-Git exported package passes; a corrupted census receipt rejects.
- The emitted program exactly matches pinned PR2182's `star(7)`. The original universal-connector control also passes.

Reproduce with Python 3.12 standard library:

```sh
python3.12 scripts/research_package.py --package research/seven-source-root-minimum
```

Exact base: `0fdd7d82de03e43c9e5a1000dfbcd380d1b687d2`. Only the new research package is changed. Selected construction and upstream sources remain unchanged; selected cold replay was not run.

## Coordination and credit

[Discussion2275](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/2275) records the scoped claim and completion. PR2229/2236 concern one-root sparse-output families; PR2063 concerns five-source one-root tariffs. They are distinct and credited, not resubmitted. Final overlap coverage and exact predecessor pins are in TASK.json/SOURCES.json.

Prepared by Mason Hale with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit @conorholds/PR2182 for the normalization method and star, Ross Richardson/PR934/943 for the generic connector and prefix criterion, and Douglas Colkitt/PR1185 for the six-source/Gray lineage. Apache-2.0; no independent human peer review is claimed.
